docs.title: PluginUpdateWatch
docs.text:
PluginUpdateWatch is a Paper plugin that detects installed plugins, checks supported update sources, notifies administrators when updates are available, and downloads updates on request.

Supported update sources:

  • Modrinth
  • Spigot / Spiget
  • GitHub Releases

docs.title: Current version
docs.text:
PluginUpdateWatch 1.3.3

Download PluginUpdateWatch

Download the 1.3.3 JAR or view the latest release above.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Stop your Paper server.
  2. Place PluginUpdateWatch-1.3.3.jar in the server's plugins folder.
  3. Start the server.
  4. Run /pu list as an operator.
  5. Use /pu scan to retry automatic source discovery at any time.

Note

PluginUpdateWatch does not automatically replace running plugin JARs. Downloads are placed in plugins/PluginUpdateWatch/downloads/ for you to review and install during a restart.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Automatic plugin JAR discovery
  • Exact Modrinth SHA-512 lookup
  • Modrinth, Spigot and GitHub update checks
  • Manual source configuration using only a JAR filename and source link
  • Config cleanup with backups
  • Download checksum verification
  • Download archive validation
  • Admin join notifications
  • Update statistics and diagnostics

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
PluginUpdateWatch targets Paper 1.21.11–26.3 and uses Java 21 bytecode.

See Compatibility for the exact verification scope.

docs.title: About PluginUpdateWatch
docs.text: PluginUpdateWatch is a Paper server administration plugin for discovering plugin update sources, checking for newer releases and downloading updates on request.

docs.title: Project
docs.text:
Repository:

github.com/dylantanderson92-lang/PluginUpdateWatch

docs.title: License
docs.text:
PluginUpdateWatch project code and documentation are released under the MIT License.

Third-party dependencies retain their own licenses and notices.

docs.title: Building from source
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • JDK 21+
  • Maven 3.9+

Build with:

mvn clean verify

The installable local artifact is:

target/PluginUpdateWatch-1.3.3.jar

Do not install the original- JAR.

• Add optional bStats usage metrics (plugin ID 34400), with a local metrics.enabled opt-out and support for the shared bStats opt-out.
  • Stop the metrics client on disable and avoid duplicate clients on reload.
  • Document public usage reports, reporting delays and the difference between active servers and lifetime installations.

Highlights:

  • Preserve publisher JAR filenames for GitHub and Modrinth downloads.
  • Use <PluginName>.jar when a provider supplies no filename.
  • Add /pu cleanup and /pu cleanup confirm.
  • Back up the config before confirmed cleanup.
  • Increase the plugin descriptor limit from 64 KiB to 1 MiB.
  • Show deliberately disabled plugins as informational entries.
  • Avoid duplicate console reporting for each check.

Validation documented for this release includes 89 Maven tests plus live verification on the project's two documented Paper test environments.

Highlights:

  • Added protection against JAR filenames differing only by letter case.
  • Added discovery regression tests.
  • Retained checksum enforcement and existing configuration compatibility.

Highlights:

  • Added bounded network retries.
  • Required provider checksums by default.
  • Added configurable network and download limits.
  • Improved discovery ambiguity handling.
  • Improved error classification and reporting.
  • Added archive validation hardening.
  • Added Java 21 / 25 CI coverage.

Highlights:

  • Added automatic installed-plugin detection.
  • Added exact Modrinth SHA-512 lookup.
  • Added simple jar / source manual configuration.
  • Continued support for GitHub, Spigot and Modrinth.

docs.title: Checksums & Download Security
docs.text:
Checksums are required by default.

downloads:
  require-checksum: true

This default also applies when the setting is absent from an older configuration.

docs.title: Modrinth
docs.text: Modrinth supplies SHA-512 checksums. PluginUpdateWatch verifies them.

docs.title: GitHub
docs.text: GitHub may provide SHA-256 digests for release assets. PluginUpdateWatch verifies a supplied digest when available.

docs.title: Spigot / Spiget
docs.text:
Spigot/Spiget generally does not provide a supported checksum.

With checksum enforcement enabled, an update can still be detected, but automatic download is blocked when no supported checksum is available.

docs.title: Allowing a missing checksum
docs.text:
To deliberately allow files without a checksum:

downloads:
  require-checksum: false

Then run:

/pu reload

The download is still subject to HTTPS and archive validation and is clearly reported as unverified.

Warning

Setting require-checksum: false does not bypass a malformed or mismatched checksum. If a provider supplies a checksum and it does not match, the file is rejected.

A provider checksum detects corruption. It is not an independent publisher signature or malware scan.

docs.title: Cleaning Old Config Entries
docs.text:
When a plugin JAR is renamed after an update, an older config row may point to a filename that no longer exists.

PluginUpdateWatch does not guess which new JAR replaced an old filename.

docs.title: Preview cleanup
docs.text:
Run:

/pu cleanup

This previews updates: entries whose configured files no longer exist.

docs.title: Confirm cleanup
docs.text:
After reviewing the preview:

/pu cleanup confirm

PluginUpdateWatch:

  1. Rechecks the config and missing-file list.
  2. Creates a backup under:
plugins/PluginUpdateWatch/backups/
  1. Removes exactly the previewed missing-file entries.
  2. Runs a fresh scan afterward.

docs.title: What cleanup does not remove
docs.text:
Cleanup does not delete:

  • plugin JARs
  • downloaded updates
  • plugin data folders
  • legacy plugins: settings

Existing files are retained even if a plugin is disabled, the descriptor is unreadable, or the file is a symbolic link.

Tip

If a plugin's JAR was renamed and you want to keep its configured source, update the existing jar: value before running cleanup.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
All commands use /pu, which is an alias of /pluginupdates.

Command Description /pu list Show cached update results, unresolved plugins and configuration problems /pu scan Scan installed JARs, discover sources, save config and check updates /pu check Check already-known sources without retrying automatic discovery /pu download <plugin> Download an available update /pu cleanup Preview config entries whose configured JAR files are missing /pu cleanup confirm Back up the config and remove exactly the previewed missing-file entries /pu stats Show the latest check duration, update count and provider success/failure counts /pu reload Reload the configuration and schedule a fresh scan/check

docs.title: Permission
docs.text:
All administrative commands use:

pluginupdatewatch.admin

The permission defaults to server operators.

docs.title: Console
docs.text:
Console commands omit the slash:

pu list
pu scan
pu check

docs.title: Download tab completion
docs.text: For /pu download, tab completion supplies plugin names when an available update can be downloaded.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
PluginUpdateWatch targets Paper:

1.21.11–26.3

Its plugin.yml declares:

api-version: '1.21.11'

This is the minimum API version, not an upper compatibility limit.

docs.title: Java
docs.text:
PluginUpdateWatch uses Java 21 bytecode.

Run the Java version required by your Paper build.

The documented live test environments include:

Paper Java Paper 1.21.11 build 132 Java 21 Paper 26.3 build 41 alpha Java 25

docs.title: 1.3.3 verification
docs.text:
The final local stable JAR passed the checks listed below on both documented Paper environments. It also passed bStats local/global opt-out, reload without duplicate clients, opt-out thread shutdown and normal server shutdown checks. The unit suite contains 95 tests; PR/release CI runs on Java 21 and 25.

See the build report and live test report.

docs.title: 1.3.2 verification
docs.text:
The final local 1.3.2 JAR was documented as passing:

  • startup
  • scan
  • check
  • list
  • reload
  • real Modrinth download
  • SHA-512 verification
  • missing-checksum rejection
  • cleanup preview/confirmation/backup
  • disabled-plugin informational reporting

on both documented Paper test environments.

docs.title: Scope limits
docs.text:
This does not establish compatibility with:

  • every intermediate Paper build
  • every plugin combination
  • future Paper builds
  • sustained production load

The tested Paper 26.3 build is an alpha.

No support claim is made for:

  • Folia
  • standalone Spigot

For production use, test the plugin on a server copy before deploying changes.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The configuration file is:

plugins/PluginUpdateWatch/config.yml

The current default configuration is:

check-interval-minutes: 360
notify-on-join: true
plugins-directory: ""
debug: false

metrics:
  enabled: true

network:
  connect-timeout-seconds: 10
  read-timeout-seconds: 15
  metadata-timeout-seconds: 30
  attempts: 3

downloads:
  max-size-mib: 100
  timeout-seconds: 120
  require-checksum: true

updates: []

plugins: {}

docs.title: check-interval-minutes
docs.text:
How often update checks run.

Default:

check-interval-minutes: 360

The minimum supported interval is 15 minutes.

docs.title: notify-on-join
docs.text:
Notify administrators when they join and updates are available.

notify-on-join: true

docs.title: plugins-directory
docs.text:
plugins-directory: ""

An empty value uses the parent of PluginUpdateWatch's data folder.

Relative paths use the server working directory.

docs.title: debug
docs.text:
debug: false

When enabled, an additional scan summary is logged.

docs.title: Network settings
docs.text:
network:
  connect-timeout-seconds: 10
  read-timeout-seconds: 15
  metadata-timeout-seconds: 30
  attempts: 3

Supported limits:

Setting Range connect-timeout-seconds 1–60 read-timeout-seconds 1–120 metadata-timeout-seconds 1–300 attempts 1–5

docs.title: Download settings
docs.text:
downloads:
  max-size-mib: 100
  timeout-seconds: 120
  require-checksum: true

Supported limits:

Setting Range max-size-mib 1–1024 timeout-seconds 1–1800

docs.title: Usage metrics
docs.text: Version 1.3.3 adds metrics.enabled, defaulting to true. Set it to false and run /pu reload to stop this plugin reporting. See Usage Metrics for the reported data and the global bStats opt-out. Older configs without this setting default to enabled; adding the section is optional unless you want to opt out.

docs.title: Applying changes
docs.text:
After editing the configuration, run:

/pu reload

docs.title: Downloading Updates
docs.text:
Use:

/pu download <plugin>

Downloads are saved to:

plugins/PluginUpdateWatch/downloads/

docs.title: Filenames
docs.text:
For GitHub and Modrinth, PluginUpdateWatch preserves the safe publisher asset filename.

When a provider does not supply a filename, normally Spigot, the fallback is:

<PluginName>.jar

PluginUpdateWatch does not automatically rename or delete previously downloaded files.

docs.title: Installing a downloaded update
docs.text:
1. Review the publisher's compatibility notes.
  2. Stop the server.
  3. Replace the old plugin JAR with the downloaded update.
  4. Keep the plugin's existing data/configuration folder.
  5. Restart the server.

PluginUpdateWatch does not overwrite running plugins or automatically install downloaded updates.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Downloaded JARs must contain a valid Paper/Bukkit descriptor with:

  • the expected plugin name
  • a version
  • a main class
  • the referenced main class file

Archive validation also checks entries for size, CRC, unsafe paths and duplicates.

docs.title: Download limits
docs.text:
Default settings:

downloads:
  max-size-mib: 100
  timeout-seconds: 120
  require-checksum: true

Fixed archive validation limits also apply even when the configured download size is increased.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: After PluginUpdateWatch is installed, it scans the server's original plugin JARs and tries to identify update sources.

docs.title: 1. Check the current status
docs.text:
Run:

/pu list

This shows:

  • available updates
  • unresolved plugins
  • configuration problems
  • duplicate or ambiguous JARs
  • version mismatches
  • disabled plugins as informational entries

docs.title: 2. Retry automatic discovery
docs.text:
/pu scan

A scan:

  1. Detects installed plugin JARs.
  2. Tries to discover a source.
  3. Saves detected sources.
  4. Checks for updates.

docs.title: 3. Add unresolved plugins manually
docs.text:
Open:

plugins/PluginUpdateWatch/config.yml

Add the exact JAR filename and the real project link:

updates:
  - jar: "ExamplePlugin-2.0.jar"
    source: "https://modrinth.com/plugin/example-plugin"

Then run:

/pu reload

docs.title: 4. Download an available update
docs.text:
/pu download <plugin>

Downloaded files are saved to:

plugins/PluginUpdateWatch/downloads/

Review the downloaded file, stop the server, replace the old plugin JAR, and restart.

Important

PluginUpdateWatch downloads updates on request. It does not hot-swap or automatically install plugins into a running server.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
PluginUpdateWatch targets:

  • Paper 1.21.11–26.3
  • Java compatible with your Paper version
  • PluginUpdateWatch itself uses Java 21 bytecode

Folia and standalone Spigot are not claimed as supported.

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Download PluginUpdateWatch

Choose the normal PluginUpdateWatch-<version>.jar from the release's Assets section. The .sha256 file is an optional checksum for verifying your download; it is not a plugin.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Stop the Minecraft server.
  2. Download PluginUpdateWatch-1.3.3.jar.
  3. Place the JAR in the server's plugins folder.
  4. Start the server.
  5. PluginUpdateWatch creates its configuration folder and begins a scan after startup.
  6. Run:
/pu list

Operators receive the pluginupdatewatch.admin permission by default.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
When upgrading PluginUpdateWatch:

  1. Stop the server.
  2. Remove the older PluginUpdateWatch JAR.
  3. Put the new JAR in the plugins folder.
  4. Keep the existing plugins/PluginUpdateWatch/ configuration folder.
  5. Start the server.

Existing two-field jar / source entries and older legacy plugins: entries remain supported.

Warning

Do not install the Maven original- JAR. The installable artifact is the normal PluginUpdateWatch-<version>.jar.

docs.title: Adding Plugins Manually
docs.text:
If PluginUpdateWatch cannot discover a source automatically, add the plugin to updates: manually.

Only two fields are required:

  • jar
  • source

docs.title: Modrinth
docs.text:
updates:
  - jar: "ExamplePlugin-2.0.jar"
    source: "https://modrinth.com/plugin/example-plugin"

docs.title: Spigot
docs.text:
updates:
  - jar: "SpigotPlugin.jar"
    source: "https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/example-plugin.12345/"

docs.title: GitHub
docs.text:
updates:
  - jar: "GitHubPlugin.jar"
    source: "https://github.com/owner/repository"

Use the exact installed filename, including .jar.

You do not need to add:

  • a folder path
  • the internal plugin name
  • a resource ID field
  • a provider field

Keep only one updates: section.

If the config currently contains:

updates: []

replace it with your entries.

After saving:

/pu reload

docs.title: Renamed JARs
docs.text:
If a plugin's filename changes after an update, update the corresponding jar: value.

Unmatched old entries are retained and reported so PluginUpdateWatch does not guess which plugin they belonged to.

docs.title: Usage Metrics
docs.text:
PluginUpdateWatch 1.3.3 includes the standard bStats client, registered as plugin 34400. Earlier stable versions do not report usage.

Open the usage dashboard

docs.title: What the numbers mean
docs.text: The server count measures active reporting servers. It is not a lifetime installation count, a list of server owners, or a download counter. Servers must run a build with this integration and keep metrics enabled to appear. Offline servers and servers that opt out are not counted as active.

docs.title: Data and controls
docs.text:
Metrics default to enabled, including for older configs without a metrics section. Only standard bStats data is sent: plugin/server versions, online-player count, online-mode setting, Java version, OS name/version/architecture, CPU core count and bStats' random server identifier. Aggregate charts are public.

No custom charts are added. Installed-plugin lists, source URLs, configuration contents, update results, filenames, player names and chat are not sent by PluginUpdateWatch.

To disable this plugin's metrics, add the following to plugins/PluginUpdateWatch/config.yml, then run /pu reload:

metrics:
  enabled: false

The shared plugins/bStats/config.yml opt-out is also respected. Set enabled: false there and restart the server to disable bStats globally. A report already in flight may finish when disabling the local setting.

See bStats' server-owner documentation for details.

docs.title: Reporting delay and API
docs.text:
bStats normally waits approximately 3–6 minutes before the first report and sends subsequent reports about every 30 minutes. The website publishes at hh:00 and hh:30, so the first dashboard data point can take 3–36 minutes after startup. See bStats troubleshooting. PluginUpdateWatch does not force immediate submissions or send historical installation data.

The public, read-only API can be used for a separate report or dashboard:

  • Plugin details and chart definitions
  • Chart registry
  • API documentation

Select a chart ID from the registry and request /api/v1/plugins/34400/charts/{chartId}/data. No private API key is needed for these public reports.

/pu stats continues to show local update-check diagnostics; it does not query bStats.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Use the server command version PluginUpdateWatch to confirm version 1.3.3 or later. pu version is not a supported command. Check that both the local and shared bStats settings permit reporting. For temporary diagnostics, bStats supports logFailedRequests, logSentData and logResponseStatusText in its shared config; restart after changing those settings. Turn verbose diagnostics off afterward.

A successful submission in the console and a public dashboard/API outage are separate events. An HTTP 502 while viewing public statistics does not prove that the plugin failed to submit. Avoid repeated restarts to force reports: bStats limits submissions to one per half-hour window.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
PluginUpdateWatch currently uses one administrative permission:

pluginupdatewatch.admin

It defaults to:

op

The permission allows administrators to:

  • view update results
  • scan plugins
  • check update sources
  • download plugin JARs
  • preview and confirm config cleanup
  • view statistics
  • reload configuration

The permission is declared in plugin.yml as the permission for /pluginupdates and its /pu alias.

docs.title: A plugin shows "Source not identified"
docs.text:
Add its source manually in:

plugins/PluginUpdateWatch/config.yml

Example:

updates:
  - jar: "ExamplePlugin.jar"
    source: "https://modrinth.com/plugin/example-plugin"

Then run:

/pu reload

docs.title: A JAR filename changed
docs.text:
Update the existing jar: value in the config.

PluginUpdateWatch retains unmatched old entries instead of guessing which new filename replaced them.

docs.title: Duplicate candidate JARs
docs.text:
If more than one JAR could represent the same installed plugin, PluginUpdateWatch reports the ambiguity rather than selecting one.

Stop the server, move the duplicate JAR out of the plugins folder, restart, then run:

/pu scan

Renaming a duplicate to another .jar filename in the same folder does not resolve duplicate plugin metadata. Keep only the intended copy in the plugins folder.

docs.title: Filenames differ only by case
docs.text:
Files such as:

Alpha.jar
alpha.jar

are considered ambiguous.

Stop the server and inspect the conflicting files. If they are copies of the same plugin, move the unwanted copy out of the plugins folder. If they are different plugins, give them distinct filenames that differ by more than letter case and update any corresponding jar: entries in the config. Restart the server, then run /pu scan.

docs.title: Download blocked: checksum missing
docs.text:
This is expected when:

downloads:
  require-checksum: true

and the provider does not supply a supported checksum.

Spigot/Spiget commonly falls into this category.

You can either download manually from the publisher or explicitly opt out:

downloads:
  require-checksum: false

Then run /pu reload.

docs.title: Config error
docs.text:
Correct the affected entry in config.yml and run:

/pu reload

docs.title: Provider or network error
docs.text:
Retry later with:

/pu check

Provider errors are not reported as "up to date".

docs.title: Old result marked cached
docs.text:
If a complete scan fails, /pu list can label older results as cached.

Run a new scan/check after the underlying problem is resolved.

docs.title: Need diagnostics
docs.text:
Run:

/pu stats

You can also temporarily enable:

debug: true

and then run /pu reload.

docs.title: Finding Updates
docs.text: PluginUpdateWatch checks configured sources and can also discover sources automatically.

docs.title: Automatic discovery
docs.text:
The scanner reads the original JAR files directly from the server's plugins directory.

For plugins without an explicit source, it tries:

  1. An exact SHA-512 file lookup on Modrinth.
  2. A recognized Modrinth, Spigot or GitHub link in the plugin's website metadata.

Only the file hash is sent to Modrinth. The plugin JAR itself is not uploaded.

docs.title: Safety rules
docs.text:
PluginUpdateWatch does not select projects merely because their names look similar.

It reports rather than guesses when it finds:

  • multiple matching JARs
  • filenames that differ only by case
  • installed/JAR version mismatches
  • JARs with no matching installed plugin
  • unreadable or incomplete descriptors
  • symbolic links during directory scanning

docs.title: Source errors
docs.text:
A provider error is not treated as "up to date".

When no compatible release is found, update status is reported as unknown and the release/source should be reviewed.

docs.title: Scheduled checks
docs.text:
The default check interval is:

check-interval-minutes: 360

The minimum configurable interval is 15 minutes.

docs.title: Update Sources
docs.text:
PluginUpdateWatch supports three update-source types:

  • Modrinth
  • Spigot / Spiget
  • GitHub Releases

A manual entry always uses the same basic structure:

updates:
  - jar: "ExactInstalledFilename.jar"
    source: "https://provider.example/project"

PluginUpdateWatch can also automatically discover supported source links from plugin metadata and, for Modrinth, by exact SHA-512 file lookup.

docs.title: GitHub Releases
docs.text: PluginUpdateWatch supports GitHub repositories that publish releases.

docs.title: Manual source
docs.text:
updates:
  - jar: "ExamplePlugin.jar"
    source: "https://github.com/owner/repository"

docs.title: Release selection
docs.text: PluginUpdateWatch checks the latest stable GitHub release.

docs.title: Direct downloads
docs.text:
Direct download works when exactly one JAR is present in the latest release.

If multiple JARs are present, manual selection on the release page may be required.

A GitHub release-asset URL can be used to select a specific filename in the latest release. If that asset filename changes, update the configured link.

docs.title: Checksums
docs.text:
GitHub can provide a SHA-256 digest for some release assets. PluginUpdateWatch verifies the digest when available.

No GitHub API token is required.

GitHub downloads preserve the safe publisher asset filename.

docs.title: Modrinth
docs.text: PluginUpdateWatch supports Modrinth plugin projects.

docs.title: Manual source
docs.text:
updates:
  - jar: "ExamplePlugin.jar"
    source: "https://modrinth.com/plugin/example-plugin"

docs.title: Automatic discovery
docs.text:
For plugins without an explicit source, PluginUpdateWatch can calculate the original JAR's SHA-512 hash and perform an exact Modrinth file lookup.

Only the hash is sent. The JAR is not uploaded.

docs.title: Version selection
docs.text:
PluginUpdateWatch looks for stable releases listed for:

  • the server's Minecraft version
  • Paper, Spigot or Bukkit

The primary matching JAR is preferred.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
Modrinth supplies SHA-512 checksums, which PluginUpdateWatch verifies.

For Modrinth downloads, PluginUpdateWatch preserves the safe publisher asset filename.

docs.title: Spigot / Spiget
docs.text: PluginUpdateWatch supports Spigot resource links, with update information checked through Spiget.

docs.title: Manual source
docs.text:
updates:
  - jar: "ExamplePlugin.jar"
    source: "https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/example-plugin.12345/"

docs.title: Update checks
docs.text:
Spiget may lag behind Spigot.

Premium or externally hosted resources can require manual downloading from the publisher.

docs.title: Checksums
docs.text:
Spigot/Spiget generally does not supply a supported checksum.

With the default:

downloads:
  require-checksum: true

PluginUpdateWatch can still check the resource for updates, but automatic download is blocked when no checksum is available.

To deliberately allow missing checksums:

downloads:
  require-checksum: false

Run /pu reload after changing the setting.
